Before it poured coffee,
this hanok fed politicians.
slides.subline: Onion Anguk, 5 Gyedong-gil, Jongno-gu — a hanok the Korea Tourism Organization dates to the 1920s, now a cafe that opens at 07:00 on weekdays

slides.label: When Onion Anguk opens on weekdays — 09:00 at weekends, closing at 22:00 daily, per the Korea Tourism Organization's listing, which marks it open all year round
slides.note: Sources: Korea Tourism Organization (english.visitkorea.or.kr), Onion Anguk Branch listing · KED Global / The Korea Economic Daily, September 2020 · Kinfolk, 'Ten Cafés in Seoul'

slides.title:
Three buildings that
were already used up

items.t: Seongsu — a 1970 building, a cafe since 2016
items.d: Kinfolk reports it had been a supermarket, a restaurant, a mechanics and a metal factory before the design studio Fabrikr found the space derelict

items.t: Anguk — a hanok on a Gyedong lane
items.d: The tourism listing dates the house to the 1920s and says the renovation preserved the daecheongmaru, its wooden hall floor, and the madang, its courtyard

items.t: Mia — half of a working post office
items.d: Kinfolk describes Fabrikr carrying the same approach into Onion's other sites, including one sharing a building with a post office still in service

slides.title:
It isn't a hanok cafe.
It's a method.
slides.body:
The easy reading is a pretty old house that sells good pastries. The harder one is that the house was not chosen for being pretty.

Kinfolk reports that at Onion's first site — a 1970 building in Seongsu that had been a supermarket, a restaurant, a mechanics and a metal factory — Fabrikr chose to preserve as much of the building's history as it could, leaving brickwork exposed and traces of paint and tilework intact. Anguk is that decision applied to a hanok instead of a factory. What people photograph there is wear somebody declined to sand off.
slides._note: the real message of this post

items.d: The Korea Tourism Organization lists the branch here, near Anguk Station exit 3, open year round, phone +82-70-7543-2123. The palaces are a short walk away
Per the same listing. That weekday opening is early for the neighbourhood, but hours do change — confirm on the shop's own channels before travelling

items.t: Vanilla bean latte, pandoro, salty butter bread
items.d: The tourism listing names these as the signature items. It publishes no prices, so treat figures quoted elsewhere online as unconfirmed

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal review.
Every fact here comes from published sources, checked on 2 September 2026.
slides.by:
Sources disagree on the building's age — the tourism listing says a 1920s hanok, the Korea Economic Daily calls it over a century old.
Hours and prices change, and taste is always personal.

caption:
Before it poured coffee, this hanok fed politicians.

Onion Anguk sits at 5 Gyedong-gil in Jongno. The Korea Economic Daily reports the house served as a closed-door lounge and a high-end restaurant before the cafe. It opens at 07:00 on weekdays.

Hours change, and taste is personal.
